title: Contrastive Decoding Diffing: Extracting Verbatim Finetuning Data With Just Logits
hook: You don't need the weights to steal what a model was fine-tuned on — you barely need anything. CDD recovers verbatim training text using only the logits a model already hands you.
key_points: Prior work (Minder, Dumas et al.'s 'Activation Difference Lens') showed narrow fine-tuning leaves readable traces in activation differences between base and fine-tuned models — but it needs full weight/activation access and only recovers vague, domain-level descriptions.
Contrastive Decoding Diffing (CDD) is a model-diffing method that instead works from grey-box logit access alone — no weights, no activations, no probe corpus.
By contrasting the base and fine-tuned models' next-token logits, CDD recovers actual verbatim content the fine-tuned model was trained on, not just a vague topic summary.
It extends model-diffing from a white-box research technique into a more accessible extraction attack against narrowly fine-tuned LLMs.
content_html: If a lab fine-tunes a model on sensitive or proprietary data, how much protection does keeping the weights private actually buy them? Less than it might seem, according to a model-diffing technique shared on r/MachineLearning called Contrastive Decoding Diffing (CDD).
extra_html: Earlier work (Minder, in "Narrow Finetuning Leaves Clearly Readable Traces in Activation Differences") showed that fine-tuning leaves a detectable fingerprint in the difference between a base model's and fine-tuned model's internal activations. Their method, the Activation Difference Lens (ADL), could steer generation using that difference — but it's white-box (needs full weight and activation access) and only recovers a vague, domain-level sense of what the model was tuned on. CDD pushes the same idea much further while asking for much less: using only grey-box logit access — no weights, no activations, no probe corpus of guesses — it contrasts the base and fine-tuned models' output logits to recover actual verbatim content from the fine-tuning data. That turns model diffing from a research tool for understanding fine-tuning into a practical extraction attack that works against models an attacker can only query, not inspect internally.

related.title: WARP: Weight-Space Analysis for Recovering Training Data Portfolios
related.hook: Labs rarely disclose their data mixture recipes — but WARP shows you can recover a fine-tuned model's training-domain proportions just from its released weights, no training data required.

related.title: Can vs. Will: Propensity-Aware Memorization in LLMs
related.hook: Most memorization tests ask whether you can force a model to spit out training data. This one asks a sharper question: does it leak under ordinary use? The two answers are very different.

flashcards.prompt: What access does Contrastive Decoding Diffing (CDD) need to extract training data from a fine-tuned model?
flashcards.back_html: Only grey-box logit access — the next-token probabilities the model already outputs. No weight access, no activation access, and no probe corpus of candidate documents.

flashcards.prompt: How does CDD improve on the prior white-box method (Activation Difference Lens / Minder)?

choices.text: It recovers actual verbatim fine-tuning content from logits alone, versus ADL's vague domain-level description that needed full weight/activation access
It requires more compute but achieves the same vague topic-level output as ADL
It only works when the attacker already has the original training corpus
It is strictly less powerful than ADL but easier to run

flashcards.explanation_html: ADL needed white-box weight/activation access and only surfaced a rough topic. CDD needs just logit access and recovers verbatim content — a stronger extraction result from a weaker access requirement, which is what makes it a more accessible attack.

flashcards.prompt: Why does CDD matter for model safety even though it doesn't touch weights?
flashcards.back_html: It shows that narrowly fine-tuned models can leak verbatim training content to an attacker who only has ordinary API-level logit access — no need to break in and grab weights first, lowering the bar for extraction attacks.
